subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron and heartbeat authority be implemented now as per-job/per-source provenance, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling-authority design?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing the durable authority model affects security guarantees, stored cron schema, heartbeat semantics, config migration, and compatibility for existing elevated workflows.

options.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
options.body: Treat this issue as the narrow security requirement inside the broader agent scheduling provenance design so cron, heartbeat, and future schedule APIs share one authority and audit model.

options.title: Ship a narrow cron/heartbeat marker
options.body: Add explicit elevated approval metadata only for current cron and heartbeat paths, accepting that maintainers may need a later migration into a broader scheduler API.

options.title: Fail closed until redesigned
options.body: Disable elevated execution from autonomous cron and heartbeat sources by default and require operators to opt into any future authority model after a migration notice.

recommendation.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the narrow security requirement inside the broader agent scheduling provenance design so cron, heartbeat, and future schedule APIs share one authority and audit model.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently changed the closest cron security boundary and would be best positioned to judge whether this belongs in the caller-scope path or a broader scheduler-authority design.
